glance: 400 km to Cox's Bazar by road, 10–13 hours by bus or car
inani-beach.desc: Inani sits further down the Marine Drive, and its shoreline is scattered with rocks and boulders that appear as the tide goes out, forming small pools and channels. The water is often clearer here than near town, and the crowds thinner. Late afternoon light on the rocks makes it a favourite for photographers.
blocks: How to get there
About 1 hour south of Cox's Bazar town along the Marine Drive.
Good to know
Visit at low tide to see the rocks. Rocks are slippery and sharp, so wear sandals.

glance: 400 km to Cox's Bazar by road, 10–13 hours by bus or car
coxs-bazar-beach.desc: The beach runs almost unbroken from the town southward toward Teknaf. Near town, the main access points such as Laboni, Sugandha and Kolatoli are busy with beach chairs, horse rides, photographers and snack sellers. The sand slopes so gently that waves roll in long and shallow, and sunset over the bay is a daily ritual for visitors. Walk a little away from the main points and it quickly becomes calmer.
blocks: How to get there
Fly or take a bus to Cox's Bazar town; a direct train from Dhaka via Chattogram also runs. The beach points are a short rickshaw or easy-bike ride from any hotel.
Good to know
Swim only in flagged areas and when lifeguards are on duty; rip currents are a real danger. Avoid the water when red flags are up.

glance: 400 km to Cox's Bazar by road, 10–13 hours by bus or car
coxs-bazar-teknaf-marine-drive.desc: The Marine Drive runs about 80 km from Cox's Bazar town south to Teknaf, squeezed between the Bay of Bengal on one side and forested hills on the other. Built by the army engineers and opened in 2017, it is often called the world's longest marine drive. Along the way are Himchari, Inani, Pechar Dwip, fishing villages and long empty beaches where you can stop. Many travellers simply hire a CNG or jeep and stop wherever the view is good.
blocks: How to get there
Hire a CNG, easy-bike or open jeep from Kolatoli or Sugandha point in Cox's Bazar; local buses toward Teknaf also use the road.
Good to know
Go in the afternoon to see the sun set over the sea on the way back. Do not swim at unguarded stretches; rip currents are common.

glance: 400 km to Cox's Bazar by road, 10–13 hours by bus or car
kutubdia-island.desc: Kutubdia is an island upazila in the Bay of Bengal, a short boat ride from the mainland at Magnamaghat. It is famous for its lighthouse, which guides ships toward Chattogram port. The island is covered with salt pans and shrimp ponds, and its western shore has quiet beaches and an early wind-power project. Most visitors to Cox's Bazar never come here, so it feels like a different world.
blocks: How to get there
From Cox's Bazar or Chakaria go to Magnamaghat in Pekua, then cross by speedboat or trawler to Kutubdia; use a CNG or easy-bike on the island.
Good to know
Check boat timings before crossing and avoid rough weather or cyclone signals. Accommodation is basic.

glance: 400 km to Cox's Bazar by road, 10–13 hours by bus or car
Small entry ticket; extra for the safari bus
dulahazra-safari-park.desc: Opened in 2001 in Chakaria upazila, Dulahazra was the country's first safari park. It covers about 900 hectares of rolling forest, and animals such as deer, elephants, bears, big cats and birds live in large fenced areas. Visitors walk along paths and watchtowers, and a bus ride is offered through some sections. It is a common stop on the Chattogram–Cox's Bazar highway.
blocks: How to get there
Take any Chattogram–Cox's Bazar bus and get off at Dulahazra, about 45 km north of Cox's Bazar town; the gate is beside the highway.
Good to know
Morning is best for seeing animals. Do not feed or tease them.

glance: Varies by fish; roughly 500–2000 BDT per kg
Shutki shops in Cox's Bazar town, and restaurants serving shutki bhorta
nazirartek-shutki.desc: Shutki, sun-dried fish, is a cornerstone of coastal and Chittagonian cooking, turned into fiery bhuna and bhorta. At Nazirartek near the airport, fishing families dry huge quantities of fish on bamboo racks during the dry season, an unforgettable (and strongly scented) sight. In town, shutki markets sell loitta, churi, prawns and more, vacuum-packed for travel.

glance: 400 km to Cox's Bazar by road, 10–13 hours by bus or car
maheshkhali-island.desc: Maheshkhali is the only hilly island off the Bangladesh coast. The Adinath temple, dedicated to Shiva, sits on a hill named Mainak and is a major pilgrimage site, especially during the Shivaratri fair. The island also has Buddhist temples, salt fields, betel-leaf gardens and mangrove-lined channels. The speedboat ride across from Cox's Bazar's 6 No. Jetty is short and lively.
blocks: How to get there
Speedboat or trawler from the 6 No. Jetty (Kasturi Ghat) in Cox's Bazar, then a rickshaw or easy-bike to the temple.
Good to know
Wear a life jacket on the speedboat and avoid crossings in rough weather. Remove shoes at the temple.

glance: Gorakghata bazar and paan boroj areas on Maheshkhali island (a short speedboat ride from Cox's Bazar's 6 No. Jetty)
maheshkhali-paan.desc: Paan growing is one of the oldest livelihoods on Maheshkhali, the country's only hilly island. Farmers raise the vines in shaded bamboo enclosures called boroj on the slopes, and the leaf is prized for being sweet rather than sharp. A folk song even sings of Maheshkhali's paan, and visitors often pick up a bundle on the way back from the island.

glance: Rakhine-run restaurants on Buddhist Temple Road (such as Khing Mundi), and the Burmese Market in Tekpara, Cox's Bazar town
coxs-bazar-rakhine-food.desc: Cox's Bazar has an old Rakhine community, and a few family-run eateries cook their food: mundi rice-noodle soup, binni (sticky) rice, hill-style chicken curry and salads of squid or snail. Mundi is best on a winter evening. The Burmese Market in Tekpara, begun in 1962, is the place to buy tangy Myanmar-style pickles to take home.

glance: 400 km to Cox's Bazar by road, 10–13 hours by bus or car
ramkot-banashram-ramu.desc: Ramu, just north of Cox's Bazar, has long been a centre of Barua and Rakhine Buddhism, with dozens of viharas and kyangs. Ramkot (Rangkut) Banashram, on a forested hill, is known as the oldest Buddhist monastery in Bangladesh, and tradition links its founding to the emperor Ashoka. Elsewhere in Ramu are colourful wooden and modern temples, including a giant reclining Buddha. Many temples were attacked in 2012 and later rebuilt, and they welcome respectful visitors.
blocks: How to get there
Ramu is about 30 minutes by bus or CNG from Cox's Bazar on the Chattogram road; hire a CNG or easy-bike there to go between the temples.
Good to know
Remove shoes before entering and dress modestly. Probarona Purnima (October) brings lantern festivals to Ramu.

glance: 400 km to Cox's Bazar by road, 10–13 hours by bus or car
ramu-probarona-fanush.desc: Ramu, a short drive from Cox's Bazar, has a long Buddhist history and many viharas, some dating back centuries, as well as a large reclining Buddha statue. At Probarona Purnima, which marks the end of the monastic rainy-season retreat in October, the community releases paper lanterns (fanush) into the night sky. Ramu is also known for floating decorated model boats on the Bakkhali river during the festival. Visitors are welcome if they are respectful.
blocks: How to get there
About 30–40 minutes by CNG or bus from Cox's Bazar town.
Good to know
Remove shoes in temples and ask before photographing monks or rituals.

glance: About 400–600 BDT per person for a seafood meal
Rice hotels around Dolphin Mor, Saymon Road and Police Station Road, Cox's Bazar town (Jhaubon on Saymon Road is known for loitta fry)
coxs-bazar-loitta-fry.desc: Loitta (Bombay duck) is a soft, almost boneless sea fish that is battered and fried until crisp, while coral, the local name for barramundi, goes into a light curry. Rice hotels in town serve them with dal, vegetables and a spread of bhortas made from shutki, shrimp and banana blossom. It is the everyday seafood lunch most visitors come back for.

glance: 400 km to Cox's Bazar by road, 10–13 hours by bus or car
shah-porir-dwip.desc: Shah Porir Dwip lies at the far end of Teknaf, where the Naf River meets the Bay of Bengal and Myanmar's hills rise across the water. It was once a separate island and is now joined to the mainland by road. The beach is long and empty, and fishing boats come and go from its ghats. Few tourists go beyond Teknaf, so it feels very remote.
blocks: How to get there
From Cox's Bazar go to Teknaf by bus or along the Marine Drive, then take a CNG or easy-bike south to Shah Porir Dwip.
Good to know
This is a border area: carry ID, follow BGB instructions and do not go near the river at night.

glance: Varies widely by fish; agree the price per piece or per kg before frying
Stalls near Sugandha and Kolatoli beach points
coxs-bazar-seafood-fry.desc: Along Sugandha and Kolatoli, stalls display the day's catch on ice: rupchanda (pomfret), coral fish, prawns, crabs, squid and more. You choose, they weigh it, rub it with chilli and spices and fry it on the spot. It is the classic evening snack after watching the sunset. Prices depend on the size and type of fish.

glance: 400 km to Cox's Bazar by road, 10–13 hours by bus or car
st-martins-island.desc: St. Martin's is a small island in the far south of the Bay of Bengal, known locally as Narikel Jinjira, 'coconut island'. Its shores are lined with coral rubble, rocky pools and palms, and the water is clearer than anywhere else on the Bangladeshi coast. Fishing is the main livelihood, and grilled fish at the jetty is a classic island meal. The island is ecologically sensitive and protected, which is why visits are now tightly controlled. Chhera Dwip, a tiny islet at its southern tip, can be reached on foot at low tide.
blocks: How to get there
When open to tourists, ships run to the island in season; recently they have departed from Cox's Bazar town rather than Teknaf. Check current routes before booking.
Good to know

Since 2024 the government has restricted tourism here to a short winter window with a daily visitor cap, online registration and limits on overnight stays. Rules change each season, so check official notices before planning. Never touch or take coral, avoid plastic, and do not ride vehicles on the beach. Do not travel in rough weather or during cyclone signals.

glance: 400 km to Cox's Bazar by road, 10–13 hours by bus or car
sonadia-island.desc: Sonadia lies just off Maheshkhali and has almost no tourist infrastructure. Its beaches are wide and quiet, with red crabs scuttling across the sand, and the surrounding mudflats are known to birdwatchers as a winter stop for migratory shorebirds. Sea turtles have also nested on its shores. Visiting feels like seeing the coast before it was built up.
blocks: How to get there
Reserve a trawler from Cox's Bazar or travel via Maheshkhali; arrange the boat in advance with a local guide.
Good to know
There are no proper facilities, so carry water and food and take all rubbish back. Check the weather and avoid monsoon crossings.

himchari.desc: Himchari lies along the Marine Drive a short ride south of town, where the coastal hills of the national park come right down to the shore. A long staircase leads up to a viewpoint looking across the sand and surf in both directions. A small waterfall trickles off the hillside, flowing best in the rainy months. The drive itself, with sea on one side and hills on the other, is one of the best parts of the trip.
blocks: How to get there
About 30 minutes south of Kolatoli along the Marine Drive by CNG, jeep or open-top 'chander gari'.
Good to know
Combine with Inani on the same half-day trip. The staircase is steep, so take it slowly in the heat.
